overview:
The last quarter redrew the map. OpenAI stopped being just a model supplier and became a direct competitor: its Presence platform (launched 22 July) sells managed customer-facing voice and chat agents to enterprises, with BBVA, SoftBank and IAG already named and OpenAI claiming its own support line resolves 75% of issues on it. Public markets noticed — HubSpot dropped 12.7% on the news. At the same time the money got bigger everywhere else: Sierra raised $950M at a $15B valuation (May), Salesforce is closing its ~$3.6B acquisition of Fin (the company formerly known as Intercom, announced 15 June), and Decagon sits at $4.5B after January's $250M Series D — with Newcomer reporting it has now passed $100M in annualised revenue.
The 12-month podcast scan tells the mindshare story behind those numbers. Decagon drew 175 mentions across the tracked shows with the best sentiment profile in the set (136 positive, 34 neutral, 5 negative — 78% positive), and August's a16z interview on its 90%-open-source stack is echoing across re-uploads and clip channels. Sierra (165) leads raw volume and just became Acquired's presenting partner, Fin's 145 is heavily acquisition-driven news chatter, and Agentforce (74) trails despite Salesforce's marketing weight. Hosts and guests consistently frame Decagon around execution: the forward-deployed-engineering debate, the 90%-open-source serving stack, and founder-led deployment discipline.
Two structural shifts run under everything: pricing is moving to outcomes (Fin at $0.99 per resolution, Zendesk at $1.50–2.00, Salesforce introducing pay-per-resolution), and voice has become the primary battleground, with every major player shipping voice capability in an eight-week window. Salesforce's own research says AI-agent adoption in service organisations jumped from 39% to 66% year on year — the market is no longer early; it is contested.

themes.name: Frontier labs enter the arena
themes.description: OpenAI's Presence turns the biggest model vendor into a direct competitor for enterprise customer-facing agents, sold through a consulting-led motion with PwC and its Bain-backed deployment company. Anthropic is signing enterprise CX-adjacent deals of its own. Every specialist now competes with its (potential) supplier.

evidence.label: OpenAI launches Presence with BBVA, SoftBank and IAG; own support line resolves 75% of issues
Presence is consulting-led, not self-service — deployed via OpenAI's services arm
HubSpot fell 12.7% as analysts pointed at OpenAI's agent push
Amex GBT brings Claude into business-travel servicing

themes.name: Consolidation and mega-rounds at the top
themes.description: The category's leaders are being capitalised like platforms, not features: Sierra at $15B, Decagon at $4.5B and past $100M ARR, Salesforce paying ~$3.6B for Fin. Sub-scale specialists (Cresta's $270M total raised is now an order of magnitude behind) face a squeeze between the giants and the labs.

evidence.label: Sierra raises $950M at $15B; 40% of the Fortune 50, ~$150M ARR
Salesforce to acquire Fin (formerly Intercom) for ~$3.6B, announced 15 June 2026
Decagon's $250M Series D at $4.5B valuation
Newcomer: Decagon passes $100M annualised revenue

themes.name: Outcome-based pricing becomes the default ask
themes.description: Per-resolution pricing has moved from experiment to expectation in one year: Fin charges $0.99 per resolution, Zendesk $1.50–2.00, HubSpot ~$0.50, and Salesforce has introduced pay-per-resolution for Help Agent after two earlier pricing models. Buyers now open negotiations asking what a resolution costs — and how the vendor counts one.

evidence.label: Per-resolution rates now run ~$0.50–$2.00 across major vendors
Salesforce's pricing evolution: conversations → Flex Credits → pay-per-resolution
Bessemer: how four AI founders (incl. Ada's) landed on durable monetisation

themes.name: Voice is the new battleground
themes.description: In eight weeks: Sierra shipped Voice Personas and out-of-the-box IVR navigation, Salesforce launched Agentforce Voice for Japan, PolyAI released a new realtime conversation model, OpenAI detailed its turnless GPT-Live architecture, and ByteDance shipped a full-duplex model. Voice quality is commoditising fast — differentiation is moving to what the agent can actually resolve on the call.

evidence.label: Sierra launches Voice Personas
Salesforce launches Agentforce Voice for Japan on Kotoba tech
PolyAI ships a new realtime voice conversation model
OpenAI's GPT-Live: turnless, low-latency voice architecture

themes.name: Model costs collapse — and open source becomes strategy
themes.description: DeepSeek's V4 Pro reaches near-frontier quality at commodity prices, OpenAI cut GPT-5.6 pricing again, and Decagon now runs 90% of its platform on fine-tuned open-source models. But free-at-scale is ending: DeepSeek has signalled a significant price rise and Alibaba is moving Qwen to a royalty model for large users. Owning your serving stack is becoming a margin and independence story, not just an engineering choice.

evidence.label: Decagon runs 90% of enterprise workflow on fine-tuned open-source models
DeepSeek ships V4 Pro, closing on frontier tier at commodity prices
DeepSeek signals a 'significant' price increase
Alibaba weighs royalty charges for big users of open-source Qwen

themes.name: From deflection to proactive, long-running agents
themes.description: The product frontier has moved past answering inbound tickets. Sierra's Horizon agents pursue outcomes over days or months and its Plaid deal connects agents to bank accounts mid-conversation; Decagon's Browser Actions and Forethought's Browser Agents act across any web system; Agentforce Coworker embeds agents in every workflow; the US Army is deploying agents at DoD Impact Level 5. Agents are becoming actors with system access, not chat windows.

evidence.label: Sierra's long-running Horizon agents chase outcomes over weeks
Decagon launches Browser Actions — agents that act across any web system
Sierra × Plaid: agents connect to bank accounts mid-conversation
US Army HRC deploys Agentforce after IL5 authorisation

convergence: Everyone is converging on the same prize — owning the enterprise customer conversation — from different directions. The labs are coming down the stack (OpenAI's Presence sells finished agents, not tokens; Anthropic sells services through enterprise deals), the incumbents are buying their way in (Salesforce absorbing Fin into Agentforce), and the specialists are expanding sideways: Sierra from support into proactive sales, mortgages and insurance claims; Decagon into browser-level actions across any system; Parloa and PolyAI up from voice into full platforms. Meanwhile the defensible edges are shifting from model quality — which is commoditising from above (GPT-5.6 price cuts) and below (DeepSeek, Qwen) — to distribution, compliance and locality: SAP certification and EU data sovereignty for Parloa and Mistral in Europe, IL5 authorisation for Salesforce in government, Japanese-language voice for the Japan fight. The collision course is set: within a year the same Fortune 500 RFP will regularly feature a frontier lab, a CRM incumbent and two specialists, all quoting per-resolution prices.

predictions.claim: Another top-ten CX AI specialist is acquired by an incumbent platform (CRM, CCaaS or cloud)
predictions.rationale: Salesforce's ~$3.6B Fin deal repriced the category and left every other incumbent without an agent-native asset, while sub-scale specialists face rising cost of competing.

predictions.claim: Per-resolution or outcome-based pricing becomes table stakes in enterprise deals
predictions.rationale: Fin, Zendesk, HubSpot and now Salesforce all sell resolution-priced offerings, and buyers are anchoring negotiations on cost-per-outcome.

predictions.claim: OpenAI Presence wins marquee logos but stays services-led — specialists keep winning product-led deployments under the Fortune 100
predictions.rationale: Presence is not self-service and deploys through OpenAI's consulting arm with partners like PwC, a motion that scales to dozens of accounts, not thousands.

predictions.claim: Voice overtakes chat as the primary battleground in new enterprise CX AI evaluations
predictions.rationale: Every major player shipped voice capability within eight weeks this summer, and realtime speech models (GPT-Live, SeedRealtime, PolyAI) have closed the naturalness gap that kept voice second.

predictions.claim: Fine-tuned open-source serving stacks become the norm among CX AI specialists
predictions.rationale: Decagon's 90%-open-source stack shows the economics work at enterprise grade, and PolyAI's Raven post-training claims point the same way — though Qwen royalties and DeepSeek's price rise show 'open' won't mean free at scale.
